claims.head: In close vs. From distance
claims.body: The Rangers get in close, but the Flames mostly shoot from distance. The Rangers are one of the league’s best for shots from in close, and Calgary is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Rangers to do more of their damage around the net.

CGY.head: The Flames have a hill to climb
CGY.body: Even though Calgary has home-ice advantage, the Rangers have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Flames can pull it off if they keep the shots coming.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Rangers?
paras: The Flames (7-9-1) lost 5-3 to Anaheim on Friday, while the Rangers have won two in a row. Going in, the Rangers are third in the Metropolitan (tied for 14th in the NHL) and the Flames fifth in the Pacific (tied for 24th).

The Rangers lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (2nd lowest), forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd) and get a lot of their shots blocked (32nd). The Flames play some of the league’s fastest games (2nd) and have struggled on the power play (30th). They also take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd), so good looks are likely to be hard to come by for them. Calgary has scored 2.47 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. The Rangers get in close, but the Flames mostly shoot from distance.

Adam Fox (2 G / 19 A / 21 P in 17 GP) leads the Rangers in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Alexis Lafrenière (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 17 GP) has a team-high nine goals, with five goals in six games against Calgary since 2023-24. For the Flames, Joel Farabee (6 G / 10 A / 16 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Matt Coronato (3 G / 11 A / 14 P in 17 GP) is next in line.
Dylan Garand (6-6-1 / .906 SV% in 11 GS) is in line to start for the Rangers. Dustin Wolf (3-5-1 / .869 SV% in 9 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Calgary, but will likely start.
At home, Ryan Huska likes to send Farabee, Backlund and Coronato out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Kartye, Miller and Perreault.

items.text: The Rangers are newly without Sean Durzi, and have been without Matthew Robertson for several games.
The Flames are newly without Kevin Bahl, have been without Samuel Honzek and Connor Zary for several games, and have had to make do without Jonathan Huberdeau all season.
Pavel Dorofeyev has five goals on chances worth about 7.2 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Matt Rempe plays in his hometown, Calgary.
